ideas.name: Minimal-fix GRPO: LOO / Dr.GRPO mean subtraction, one fixed global scale, constant-denominator (seq-mean-token-sum-norm) aggregation
aliases: Scale-fixed RLOO variant (a) (Dr. GRPO made unbiased end-to-end)
Constant loss aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with a fixed loss_scale_factor
ideas.formula:
mean_{-i} = (1/(n-1)) sum_{j != i, same prompt} r_j
A_i = (r_i - mean_{-i}) / c,   c = 18 fixed (measured RMS within-group std of the baseline run)      [verl 'rloo' = c*A_i; 'drgrpo' = grpo with norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=False = (n-1)/n * c*A_i, same direction]
Aggregation: actor.loss_agg_mode = seq-mean-token-sum-norm. VERIFIED for this fork's legacy path (trainer.use_legacy_worker_impl=auto -> fsdp_workers -> DataParallelPPOActor): config.global_batch_info is never filled (only workers/utils/losses.py:105-108 fills it, new-engine path), so agg_loss (core_algos.py:1061-1073) gets global_batch_size=None -> seq_mask.sum()=1 per one-sequence micro-batch, and loss_scale_factor=None -> S = loss_mask.shape[-1] = rollout.response_length, to which agent_loop pads every response (agent_loop.py:548-553) -- a constant (32000 per the proposers' measurements / hardtest scripts; 16000 in the current synthetic script: check data.max_response_length). actor.loss_scale_factor is IGNORED on this path. The micro-batch loss is then multiplied by 1/G (G = gradient_accumulation, constant, dp_actor.py:583-585) and DP-averaged.
Applied gradient (ratio == 1, fully on-policy):
  g_hat = (1/(N G S c)) * sum_{i=1..N} (r_i - mean_{-i}) * sum_t grad log pi(y_it | x_i, y_i<t)     -- every weight a constant
KL term: aggregated by the same agg_loss call -> (1/S) sum_t kl_t per sequence; with A in GRPO-like units (RMS |A| ~ 1) keep kl_loss_coef = 0.001 so the baseline's per-token pg:KL ratio is preserved.
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: J, exactly: E[g_hat] = kappa grad J with kappa = 1/(G S c), a fixed hyperparameter (times (n-1)/n for drgrpo). The KL-to-reference term is a separate, unchanged regularizer, not part of the J estimator.
ideas.unbiasedness_argument:
AUDIT of what is actually running (all items verified in the fork): (0) the baseline is NOT batch token-mean: ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1, use_dynamic_bsz=false, legacy worker -> agg_loss('token-mean') with batch_num_tokens=None divides by the token count of the one-sequence micro-batch -> per-sequence weight w_i = 1/L_i (seq-mean-token-mean), x1/G x DP-mean. Empirical confirmation (wandb run aiv6wdim, step 81): actor/pg_loss = 7.2e-07 while sum_i A_i L_i / sum_i L_i = +0.019; a batch token-mean would log -0.019 exactly; per-sequence weighting logs -(1/N) sum_i A_i = 0 to float precision because GRPO advantages sum to 0 per group. (1) Self-inclusion in the group mean: r_i - mean_g = (n-1)/n (r_i - mean_{-i}); constant factor, harmless. (2) Division by std_g (ddof=1, computed from the 8 samples INCLUDING r_i): conditional on y_{-i} the map r_i -> (r_i - mean)/(s+eps) is nonlinear and bounded, |A_i| <= (n-1)/sqrt(n) = 2.475 (exactly the measured +2.47 on the 50.15 outlier), so E_{y_i}[A_i S_i | y_{-i}] = grad E_{y_i}[phi_{y_{-i}}(r(y_i))]: the gradient of a sample-dependent nonlinear transform of the reward -> DIRECTION bias within the prompt plus a sample-dependent cross-prompt weight ~1/sigma_x. Exact enumeration of all 8^4 groups on a 4-sequence toy policy: cos(E[g], grad J_x) = 0.983-0.998 with per-coordinate kappa spread 0.27-0.62 inside one prompt; toy MC with continuous rewards: best-fit residual 1.8% vs 0.1% MC floor. Not fixable by rescaling. (3a) The running w_i = 1/L_i: E[(r_i - b) S_i / L_i] = grad E_y[(r(y) - b)/L(y)] -- the gradient of reward-per-token, and the baseline term -b grad E[1/L] is NOT zero: with b > 0 responses with r > b are pushed shorter and r < b longer (Dr.GRPO's length bias, exact for this code path; measured within-group corr(r, L) = -0.14 makes it bite). Toy: cos 0.934-0.987, 44% residual, length-controlling coordinates down-weighted ~2x. (3b) Global batch token-mean (what the task statement assumed; the new-engine path) is a ratio estimator with the own L_i at weight ~1/64: toy MC cos > 0.99999, negligible but strictly sample-dependent. (4) reinforce_plus_plus_baseline whitening: token-weighted batch mean mu = sum L_i a_i / sum L_i has E[mu] != 0 whenever corr(a, L) != 0 (-0.14 -> every advantage lifted -> the measured 5% sign flips) and the batch sd gives a per-STEP sample-dependent kappa_t (toy: 0.04 vs 0.67 across reward regimes) that AdamW beta2 = 0.999 (~1000-step v window) does not undo. Reject. (5) PPO clip: on_policy (one mini-batch, ppo_epochs=1) -> old_log_prob = log_prob.detach() -> ratio == 1 exactly -> clip/dual-clip never active (pg_clipfrac = 0). No bias while ppo_mini_batch_size == train_batch_size. (6) eps = 1e-6: all-equal groups give numerator 0 -> A = 0; irrelevant otherwise. (7) grad_clip = 1.0: inactive at baseline norms 0.1-0.5; any fix must keep it so, or clipping becomes an active sample-dependent rescale.
MINIMAL FIX = remove (2) and (3a) and make the denominator a constant. PROOF: conditional on y_{-i}, E_{y_i}[(r_i - mean_{-i}) S_i] = sum_y (r(y) - mean_{-i}) grad pi(y|x) = grad J_x - mean_{-i} grad(sum_y pi(y|x)) = grad J_x. Summing the n samples of a group: n grad J_x. The 8 prompts per step are a uniform shuffle of the 200, so E over x is E_{x~D}. Hence E[g_hat] = (8n/(N G S c)) grad J = (1/(G S c)) grad J. Toy exact enumeration: per-coordinate ratio E[g]/grad J = 8.000 on every coordinate for rloo and 7.000 for drgrpo.
ideas.variance_argument: Var[g_hat] ~ (1/(G S c))^2 sum_i E[(r_i - mean_{-i})^2 ||S_i||^2] ~ sum_x n^2/(n-1) sigma_x^2 E||S||^2. Versus GRPO: (a) prompt contributions scale with sigma_x^2 -- a 90th-percentile prompt (sigma 26) carries ~3.7x a median one (13.5); GRPO equalized these at the price of the direction bias; (b) flat groups contribute exactly 0 and near-flat groups ~(0.15/18)^2 instead of 2.47^2: a ~1e5 reduction of the variance injected by the 4% near-flat groups, which under GRPO are pure noise at full amplitude. Versus the running 1/L_i weighting: E||S_i||^2 ~ L_i v_tok (token scores roughly uncorrelated), so a sequence's gradient share becomes ~L_i/S instead of ~1/L_i: 16k-token responses contribute ~1.8x a 9k one and 1k-token ones ~9x less than before -- the true REINFORCE variance profile the 1/L_i weighting was hiding while adding the length bias. The LOO mean is the minimum-variance baseline among per-prompt constants built from the other samples' rewards (its own variance sigma_x^2/(n-1) = 14% of the per-sample variance; the oracle mean mu_x is the floor at 0.875x RLOO's proxy). Gradient scale: with RMS|A| ~ 1 and S = 32000 the per-sequence gradient is ~L_i/S times the baseline's per-sequence token-mean one, so the raw grad norm lands at ~0.3x the baseline's (0.03-0.15): clipping stays inactive and Adam cancels the constant (per-element |g| ~ 1e-6 >> eps = 1e-8).
ideas.continuous_friendliness: A_i is linear in r_i: one point of partial credit is always worth 1/c advantage units regardless of the group's spread. [50,50,50,50,50,50,50.15,50] -> A = +0.008 for the 50.15 (rloo; +0.0075 drgrpo) versus GRPO's +2.47, and -0.001 for the others; all-equal groups -> 0; 100 vs seven 0s -> 100/18 = 5.6 (uncapped, unlike GRPO's 2.47 ceiling); a 30-point-spread group gets ~200x the signal of a 0.15-point one, as E[r] dictates. The scale is identical across prompts and steps; no sign flips; no cross-prompt or cross-step coupling. Downside: no per-prompt normalization, so prompts with naturally large spread dominate a step (ideas rloo-prompt-scale and is-prompt-sampling give legal versions of that normalization).

ideas.risks: (1) Early training (83% flat groups in steps 1-20): with a constant scale the raw gradient is small and AdamW's v (beta2 = 0.999, window >> the 400-step run) lags when spreads grow later -> the effective step size drifts upward mid-run; rloo-lagged-scale fixes this legitimately. (2) High-spread prompts dominate and near-zero-spread prompts contribute nothing (correct for J, but slower on 'almost solved' prompts than GRPO). (3) Long responses dominate the gradient (true REINFORCE variance); if clipping triggers, shrink A by a constant, never reinstate a sample-dependent normalizer. (4) KL is now token-sum-weighted per sequence (long responses carry more KL); any constant folded into A must also be folded into kl_loss_coef or the KL is silently re-weighted. (5) If the run ever moves to the new engine worker (use_legacy_worker_impl=disable) actor.loss_scale_factor becomes live and the batch-level denominators change; re-check the constants. (6) Dr.GRPO reports that response-length behaviour changes once the 1/L_i weight is removed (responses stop being penalized for length); watch the truncation rate at the response budget. (7) pg_loss / grad_norm dashboards become non-comparable with the baseline (harmless for AdamW). (8) Lowering ppo_mini_batch_size below the batch re-activates PPO clipping = a biased surrogate.

ideas.name: RLOO divided by a lagged global scale: EMA of PAST steps' within-group spread (fixed-constant and leave-one-group-out variants)
aliases: Lagged global reward scale with LOO baseline (RLOO / sigma_bar_{t-1})
History-scaled RLOO variant (a): lagged global scale
Scale-fixed RLOO variants (b) EMA of past steps and (c) leave-one-group-out
leave-one-out mean divided by lagged RMS spread
ideas.formula:
Driver-side state, persisted across steps: v_bar = EMA of within-group reward VARIANCE (init v_bar = s0^2, s0 = 18 measured; (100/sqrt(12))^2 if nothing is known).
Step t, BEFORE touching the state:
  c_t = max(sqrt(v_bar), c_min)                      # c_min ~ 3-5 reward points, fixed
  A_i = (r_i - mean_{-i}) / c_t = (n/(n-1)) (r_i - mean_g) / c_t        (flat groups -> A = 0 exactly)
AFTER the step's advantages are computed (never before):
  v_now = mean over this step's groups of s_g^2 (ddof=1; flat groups count as 0)
  v_bar <- beta v_bar + (1-beta) v_now,   beta in [0.9, 0.98]  (beta = 1 recovers rloo-const's fixed c)
Stateless alternative (no memory): c_{-g} = max(c_min, sqrt(mean over the OTHER 7 groups g' of the step of (r_j - mean_{g'})^2)) and A_i = (r_i - mean_{-i}) / c_{-g}.
Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with constant S (rloo-const). g_hat = (1/(N G S c_t)) sum_i (r_i - mean_{-i}) sum_t grad log pi(y_it | x_i, y_i<t).
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: J, conditionally on the past: E[g_hat | F_{t-1}] = kappa_t grad J(theta_t) with kappa_t = 1/(G S c_t) > 0 F_{t-1}-measurable (previous batches + fixed s0, c_min, beta), exactly as the definition allows. Leave-one-group-out: kappa = E[1/c_{-g}], theta-dependent but not a function of group g's own samples (the 8 prompts of a step are drawn without replacement, a negligible coupling with x_g).
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: Let F_{t-1} be everything observed before step t; c_t is F_{t-1}-measurable. Conditional on F_{t-1} and theta_t, the LOO baseline is independent of y_i given x, so E[mean_{-i} S_i] = 0 and E[r_i S_i] = grad J_x (score-function identity; ratio == 1 so the surrogate's gradient is exactly REINFORCE's). Summing the N samples with x ~ uniform over the 200 prompts: E[g_hat | F_{t-1}] = (1/(G S c_t)) grad J. Two things would break this: (a) including the current step's groups in v_bar before computing A (a 'running std including the current batch'): the leak weight is (1-beta)/8 groups ~ 1% per step -- small but nonzero, and strictly lagging costs nothing; (b) any per-sample or per-batch denominator (GRPO's per-group s_g, batch whitening, the batch's token count): in aggregate GRPO's 1/s_g is a per-step sample-dependent scale correlated with the numerator, a global, milder version of the per-group defect. Lagging decorrelates scale and numerator. For c_{-g}: it depends only on the other groups' samples, which are independent of (x_g, y_g) given the prompts, so the factor pulls out of E_{y_g}; a floor is needed when several other groups are flat.
ideas.variance_argument: Within a step, dividing all advantages by one scalar leaves every group's signal-to-noise ratio unchanged (signal and sampling noise scale together); the reward-unit weighting across groups is the one whose sum is grad J. GRPO's per-group 1/s_g instead gives a group with s_g = 0.8 (the 4% of non-flat groups spanning < 2 points) a weight c_t/s_g >= 20x an average group's, amplifying signal and noise 20x: the [50,...,50.15,50] group gets |A| = 2.47 under GRPO versus 0.009 here (270x). Across steps, GRPO pins RMS(A) ~ 1 using the batch's own spread; here it floats. Measured on the 105 saved steps, beta = 0.9: token-weighted RMS(A) median 0.91 (GRPO 0.90), p10 0.28, p90 1.26, max 1.78; per-step ratio RMS(A)/RMS(A_grpo) median 1.08, p90 1.54, max 3.5; 12/105 steps have RMS > 1.25. beta = 0.98: max 1.66. Fixed c = 18: median 0.81, p90 1.15, max 1.47 -- nearly as good because c drifted only 18 -> 14-16 over 105 steps (per-25-step-block RMS std 9.8 -> 15.7 -> 18.4 -> 16.4). c_t estimated from 8 groups per step has ~25% relative noise; an EMA with a = 1-beta = 0.1 (~10-step window) cuts it to ~8%, still fully predetermined. Why a scale-only change matters: AdamW beta2 = 0.999 averages v over ~1000 steps (longer than the run), so it does NOT normalize per-step gradient scale; a constant kappa is cancelled by Adam except through eps (per-element |g| ~ 3e-6 >> 1e-8), and the scale acts only through grad_clip (upper side) and the PG:KL ratio inside the gradient (Adam does not cancel a ratio between two terms). An EMA horizon of 10-50 steps tracks the flat -> spread transition (83% flat groups in steps 1-20 vs 24% overall), faster than Adam can. Gradient-norm spread across steps is roughly +/-50% around the baseline's (median 0.1-0.5, clip 1.0), so clipping stays rare and kl_loss_coef = 0.001 keeps its calibrated meaning.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Advantages are linear in reward differences inside a step: 0.15 points -> 0.009; 100 vs seven 0s -> 6.25 at c = 16; GRPO caps every sample at 2.47 whether the gap was 0.15 or 100 points, this keeps that information (max |A| per step: median 3.2, p90 4.9, max 6.1 at c = 16). Flat groups -> exactly 0. Across prompts the scale is in common reward units: a prompt spanning 0-100 contributes ~10x one spanning 0-10, the J-consistent weighting. Across time one global c_t slowly tracks the reward spread, so early tiny-spread steps are not systematically under-weighted relative to later ones, and c_min prevents amplifying a near-flat regime into GRPO-like noise. This is the entry that most directly replaces GRPO's step-size normalization without any per-group division.
ideas.verl_sketch:
Same plugin as rloo-const with 5 lines of state:
  _STATE = {'v_bar': float(os.environ.get('LAG_S0', 18.0))**2}   # loaded from LAG_STATE_PATH json at import if present
  @register_adv_est('rloo_lagged_scale')
  def f(token_level_rewards, response_mask, index, config=None, **kw):
      scores = token_level_rewards.sum(-1); c_t = max(math.sqrt(_STATE['v_bar']), c_min)         # read BEFORE update
      inv = np.unique(index, return_inverse=True)[1]; dev = LOO deviations via the rloo_vectorized trick (core_algos.py:720-755); A = dev / c_t
      var_g = per-group ddof=1 variance of scores from bincount sums; _STATE['v_bar'] = beta*_STATE['v_bar'] + (1-beta)*var_g.mean()   # AFTER
      json.dump(_STATE, open(LAG_STATE_PATH, 'w'))     # checkpoint resume; otherwise re-init to s0 (both bias-free, a few off-scale steps)
      return A[:, None]*response_mask, A[:, None]*response_mask
Leave-one-group-out: per-group centered sum of squares SS_g via bincount; c_{-g}^2 = (sum_g' SS_g' - SS_g)/(N - n_g), floored. Config: algorithm.adv_estimator=rloo_lagged_scale actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=seq-mean-token-sum-norm kl_loss_coef=0.001; env LAG_S0=18 LAG_BETA=0.9 LAG_CMIN=3 LAG_STATE_PATH=<default_local_dir>/adv_scale.json. Log c_t, RMS(A), max|A| per step (critic/advantages/* is already logged). Offline check of the step-to-step RMS(A) distribution: replay on outputs/rollout_data_synthetic/*.jsonl with analysis/continuous_reward_advantages.py.
ideas.risks: (1) Lag: when the policy's reward spread jumps (leaving the 83%-flat early phase) c_t is behind by ~1/(1-beta) steps and gradients are 1.5-3x larger for a few steps; set the target so the baseline's median grad norm sits ~0.2-0.3, leaving 3-5x headroom to the clip. If the clip fires often the update becomes normalized-gradient descent, a sample-dependent scale again (see lagged-gradnorm-scale for the legal version). (2) c_min matters if the policy collapses to all-flat groups and then un-flattens (1/c_t would explode without it); c_min too low makes the early phase GRPO-like. (3) Does nothing about prompt-level imbalance: one 0-vs-100 group can carry most of a step (correct for J, high variance); see rloo-prompt-scale / is-prompt-sampling. (4) Resume: persist the state (tiny). (5) If the reward is rescaled (r/100), rescale s0 and c_min. (6) Leave-one-group-out: shrinks when several other groups are flat (floor it); it is mostly a step-size device -- if the AdamW lr is retuned anyway, the fixed constant may suffice; the gain is robustness across the flat -> spread transition, not a direction change.

ideas.name: RLOO with a lagged per-prompt scale from PAST visits (GRPO's cross-prompt equalization, shrunk toward the global scale and floored) -- unbiased for a reweighted J_w
aliases: Lagged per-prompt scale with shrinkage toward the global scale (and frozen fixed-w variant)
History-scaled RLOO variant (b): per-prompt historical-std weighting with a floor
LOO-scale GRPO (stateless cross-fit variant, status flagged)
ideas.formula:
Stable prompt key x = hash of the un-padded prompt token ids (the per-step uid is a fresh uuid4 and is NOT stable across visits).
Past visits of x (steps < t only): within-group variances s_{x,1}^2 .. s_{x,m_x}^2 (equivalently an EMA of std_g with a = 0.5).
  v_x = (k0 v_bar + sum_k s_{x,k}^2) / (k0 + m_x)      # v_bar = rloo-lagged-scale's global lagged EMA; k0 = 2-3 pseudo-visits; m_x = 0 at first visit -> v_x = v_bar
  s_x = max(sqrt(v_x), s_min)   (or sqrt(v_x) + eps0, additive floor)        # s_min ~ 5-10 reward points
  w(x) = 1/s_x
  A_i = w(x) (r_i - mean_{-i})
AFTER computing A: append this visit's s_g^2 to x's history; update v_bar as in rloo-lagged-scale.
Frozen variant (fixed objective): s_x^(0) from one rollout pass of the base model (or the first visit of each prompt) and never updated -> w(x) a fixed function of x. Task-known normalizer: c(x) = 100/m(x) (number of tests) -> A in 'tests passed'; same construction with w(x) = 1/c(x).
Stateless cross-fit variant (first-epoch stand-in only; see objective): A_i = (r_i - mean_{-i}) / (s_{-i} + eps0), s_{-i} = ddof=1 std of the OTHER 7 rewards (var_{-i} = ((S2 - r_i^2) - (n-1) mean_{-i}^2)/(n-2)), eps0 = 5-18.
Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with constant S (rloo-const).
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: Not J. Unbiased for J_w = E_{x~D}[ w(x) J_x(theta) ] with w(x) = 1/s_x, a strictly positive, bounded (<= 1/s_min) function of x and PAST data only; kappa = 1/(G S). In the lagged form w changes as history accumulates, so each step's estimator is unbiased for the gradient of a slowly moving J_w^{(t)} (w bounded between ~1/c_t and 1/s_min) -- there is no single fixed objective. In the frozen / task-known form w is a fixed positive function of x, J_w is a fixed objective, and its per-prompt optima coincide with J's (positive reweighting across prompts does not move the argmax of each J_x); only the relative learning rate across prompts changes. The stateless cross-fit variant has E[g_hat] = E_x[ w(x;theta) grad J_x ] with w(x;theta) = E_{y_{-i}}[1/(s_{-i}+eps0)] > 0: exact per-prompt gradient direction (toy enumeration: cos = 1.00000, per-coordinate ratio uniform to 4 digits, vs GRPO's 0.983-0.998 with 0.27-0.62 spread) but the weight depends on the current theta, so it is NOT unbiased for J nor for a fixed J_w under the task's definition.
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: s_x is F_{t-1}-measurable (previous visits of x, previous steps' v_bar, fixed k0, s_min, s0). Conditional on F_{t-1}: E[(r_i - mean_{-i}) S_i | x] = grad J_x (LOO baseline independent of y_i, E[S_i] = 0), multiplied by the predetermined scalar w(x) and summed over the n samples and the 8 uniformly drawn prompts: E[g_hat | F_{t-1}] = (8n/(N G S)) E_x[w(x) grad J_x] = (1/(G S)) grad J_w(theta), since w does not depend on theta_t and is not differentiated. This is exactly GRPO's intended objective: in expectation GRPO weights prompt x by ~1/sigma_x(theta). GRPO's version is biased because its weight 1/s_g is computed from the SAME 8 samples that appear in the numerator (relative sampling error of s_g ~1/sqrt(2(n-1)) = 27%, correlated with r_i -> audit item (2): a bounded nonlinear transform of r_i and a sample-dependent cross-prompt weight). Replacing s_g by a number fixed in advance removes both the within-prompt nonlinearity and the self-dependence; the only remaining 'bias' is the explicit, stated reweighting w(x). A flat current group gives A = 0 regardless of w.
ideas.variance_argument: Per prompt the estimator is RLOO times a constant, so per-prompt SNR equals RLOO's; what changes is the allocation of gradient budget across prompts: each prompt contributes ~unit-RMS advantages, so a single 0-vs-100 group cannot dominate a step (under J-weighting a group with s_g = 45, p99, carries 10x a median s_g = 13.5 group). The data argue for heavy shrinkage and a floor: revisits are sparse (200 prompts, 8 per step -> each prompt every ~25 steps, 4.2 visits in 105 steps; 0% of groups have a prior visit in steps 1-20, 75% in 21-40, 100% afterwards); history is a weak predictor (corr(s_prev, s_now) = 0.43-0.45 over 640 revisits; median |log(s_now/s_prev)| = 0.34, a typical factor-1.4 miss); and 23% of revisits were flat last time but non-flat now -- an unshrunk per-prompt scale would sit at s_min for those and amplify them by c/s_min, re-creating GRPO's small-gap failure one visit late. With k0 = 2 the per-prompt weight stays within ~[0.6, 1.7]x the global scale. Measured w(x)/mean(w) p10-p90: 0.37-1.43 at s_min = 5, 0.60-1.15 at s_min = 10, 0.21-1.97 at s_min = 2; 46% of groups floored at s_min = 5, 65% at s_min = 10; only 7/600 groups have current std < 2 with s_hist > 10. Tiny-spread groups: GRPO gives them RMS|A| 1.05x the overall RMS; this gives 0.03x at s_min = 5 (the floor, not the history, tames them: those prompts had median past std 2.1). A scale from one 8-sample visit has ~27% relative SE, ~19% after an a = 0.5 EMA; it perturbs weights, never direction. Cross-fit variant: the n weights differ within a group (advantages no longer sum to 0) and a single outlier [50x7, 90] gets A = 40/eps0 = 8 at eps0 = 5 (2.5 under rloo-const) -- variance, not bias, bounded by c/eps0; eps0 >= 9 caps it at <= 2x.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Linear in r within a group: a 0.15-point gap -> <= 0.15/s_min = 0.03 (GRPO: 2.47); [50x7, 50.15] on a prompt whose past spread was 0.05 -> 0.15/(0.05+5) = 0.03 with the additive floor; on a prompt with past spread 20 -> 0.006. All-equal -> 0. Across prompts advantages are comparable in 'past sigma' units -- a prompt whose rewards live in 40-60 and one living in 0-100 get similar gradient magnitude once their history is known, which is what GRPO intended; s_min sets how much equalization is allowed (s_min = 10 is nearly global, s_min = 2 lets w span 0.21-1.97x). The task-known variant is the cleanest form of per-prompt comparability, but the data show no natural unit (1273 distinct score values, 97% non-integer, per-prompt minimum observed gap median 0.1 points, p10 0.002; rollout records carry no reference score), so it needs the dataset to supply m(x) or a reference score.
ideas.risks: (1) J_w != J: low historical spread means 'consistently ~0' or 'consistently ~100', so it up-weights hopeless and solved prompts (bounded by c/s_min: 3.6x at s_min = 5, 2x at s_min = 9) and deliberately down-weights the prompts with the most headroom -- possibly the opposite of what pass-rate evaluation wants; keep s_min >= 5 and watch the floored fraction and w percentiles. (2) The lagged objective is a moving target; convergence theory for history-dependent reweighting is weak; floor and k0 are load-bearing hyperparameters. (3) The first ~25 steps have no history, so it equals rloo-lagged-scale; afterwards the per-prompt part is noisy (corr 0.45) and the benefit over the global scale on 200 prompts may be small or negative without shrinkage; with prompts >> steps most w(x) never leave their init. (4) Keying by prompt hash breaks if prompts are re-templated mid-run (benign: fresh start at v_bar); duplicates within a step (is-prompt-sampling) must update history once per group. (5) State must survive checkpoint resume. (6) Cross-fit variant: not a fixed objective; advantages do not sum to zero per group (dashboards change); an 8x advantage on a 16k-token response can trigger clipping -- use eps0 >= 9 or monitor clip frequency; without the floor it explodes on [50,...,50.15,50] (s_{-i} = 0 for the 50.15 sample).

ideas.name: Spread-proportional prompt sampling with inverse-spread advantage scaling (importance-sampled per-prompt normalization that is exactly unbiased for J)
ideas.formula:
Past-data spread s(x) = max(s_hat_t(x), s_min) as in rloo-prompt-scale (history of previous visits; global prior for never-visited prompts).
Draw the 8 prompts of step t with replacement from q_t(x) = s(x) / Z_t,  Z_t = sum_{x in D} s(x)    (optionally q_t = (1-eps) s/Z + eps/|D|).
A_i = u(x) (r_i - mean_{-i}),   u(x) = 1/(|D| q_t(x)) = Z_t/(|D| s(x))     # proportional to 1/s(x) for the pure proposal
Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with constant S.
The sampling weight and the normalization weight cancel: E[g_hat] = (1/(G S)) sum_x q_t(x) u(x) grad J_x = (1/(G S |D|)) sum_x grad J_x = (1/(G S)) grad J.
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: J (uniform over the 200 prompts), kappa = 1/(G S). (Sampling from q_t without the u(x) correction is instead unbiased for J_q with q from past data; uniform sampling with 1/s(x) scaling is rloo-prompt-scale.)
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: Standard importance sampling over the prompt distribution: for any q_t with full support fixed before the step (guaranteed by the floor s_min or the eps-mixture), E_{x~q_t}[ u(x) grad J_x ] = sum_x q_t(x) (1/(|D| q_t(x))) grad J_x = (1/|D|) sum_x grad J_x = grad J. Within a prompt, (r_i - mean_{-i}) S_i is unbiased for grad J_x (LOO argument of rloo-const). q_t and u are functions of past data only, so the per-prompt weights are uncorrelated with the current samples. Duplicated prompts in a step are two independent groups and the LOO baseline is computed per group.
ideas.variance_argument: 'Sample proportionally to contribution magnitude': if the per-prompt gradient energy scales as E||g_x||^2 ~ s(x)^2 K, the variance-optimal proposal is q ∝ sqrt(E||g_x||^2) ∝ s(x), and under it every sampled prompt contributes advantages of ~unit RMS (no dominating prompt) while rollouts are spent where the policy's outputs actually vary. Flat prompts (24% of groups, 83% early) are drawn only at the floor rate instead of producing zero-gradient groups a quarter of the time. Compared with rloo-prompt-scale it has the same per-prompt normalization but targets J, so it stops over-weighting historically low-spread (solved / hopeless) prompts. The history predicts spread only weakly (corr 0.45) -- a mediocre q costs variance, never bias, as long as u matches q.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Built for the measured regime: a continuous judge produces prompts with spread 2 and prompts with spread 26; this allocates rollouts by spread and normalizes by it, with no current-sample statistic anywhere. Tiny gaps are scaled by 1/s(x) <= 1/s_min; all-equal groups contribute 0 and reduce the prompt's future s_hat so it is drawn less.
ideas.verl_sketch: Prompt sampling: data.sampler.class_path / class_name -> a subclass of AbstractCurriculumSampler (verl/experimental/dataset/sampler.py:35; update(batch) at :39) implemented outside verl/ (e.g. FrontierSmith/analysis/spread_sampler.py); create_rl_sampler (main_ppo.py:392-410, load_extern_object) requires data.dataloader_num_workers=0 (:418); ray_trainer calls self.train_dataloader.sampler.update(batch=batch) after every step (:1683) -- update s_hat there from the batch's prompt keys (hash of data.batch['prompts'], or non_tensor_batch['index'] if the parquet gets extra_info.index) and the ddof=1 group std of token_level_scores. __iter__ yields 8 indices per step via torch.multinomial(s, 8, replacement=True); define __len__ = |D|/8 per epoch. The sampler stores u(x) for the drawn indices in a shared singleton (or writes it into non_tensor_batch); the registered estimator (rloo-prompt-scale's function reading the singleton) multiplies the RLOO deviation by u. Persist sampler state (s_hat, RNG) for StatefulDataLoader resume. Invariant log each step: mean over drawn prompts of u(x) q_t(x) |D| == 1; the fraction of flat groups should fall. Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm.
ideas.risks: A mismatch between the q actually used to draw and the u applied silently breaks unbiasedness (hence the invariant log). Starvation: prompts whose spread collapses are revisited only at the floor rate; too small an s_min starves them, too large approaches uniform sampling. Early training (most prompts flat) makes q near-uniform and u near-constant -- harmless. verl's epoch/step accounting assumes a fixed-length sampler; sampling with replacement changes the meaning of an epoch. With the eps-mixture rarely-sampled prompts carry weights up to 1/eps (keep eps >= 0.1 or rely on the floor alone). The most engineering of the top-four entries (sampler + estimator coupling + resume state).

ideas.name: RLOO-hist: leave-one-out group mean shrunk toward a per-prompt historical baseline (pseudo-count set from measured drift)
ideas.formula:
Group of n = 8 samples for prompt x, rewards r_i in [0,100].
  m_{-i} = (1/(n-1)) sum_{j != i} r_j                      # leave-one-out mean
  h(x)   = EMA (beta = 0.5) over PREVIOUS visits of x of the group mean   (undefined on the first visit)
  k      = pseudo-count fixed BEFORE the step: k = sigma2_within / tau2_drift, both estimated from PAST steps only (tau2_drift = E[(group mean at visit v - h(x) before visit v)^2], sigma2_within = E[s_g^2]); or a constant k in [1,3]
  b_i    = ((n-1) m_{-i} + k h(x)) / (n-1+k)              (k = 0 or no history -> plain RLOO, b_i = m_{-i})
  A_i    = (r_i - b_i) / c,  c the fixed (or lagged, rloo-lagged-scale) global scale; broadcast to all tokens of response i
Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with constant S. History update h(x) <- EMA with this step's group mean happens AFTER the step's advantages are computed.
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: J, kappa = 1/(G S c) (k, h, c all fixed before the step; a lagged c_t keeps it F_{t-1}-measurable).
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: b_i is a function of x, of the OTHER 7 rewards in the group, and of past batches (h, k, c) -- never of y_i. Conditioning on the other samples and the history, E_{y_i ~ pi(.|x)}[ b_i grad log pi(y_i|x) ] = b_i sum_y grad pi(y|x) = 0, hence E[ sum_i (r_i - b_i) grad log pi(y_i|x) ] = n grad J_x, and averaging over prompts with fixed weights gives kappa grad J. The division by (n-1+k) is a constant because k is set from past data. The only way to break this is to let the current group mean leak into h before use (self term), which the update order rules out. Contrast: GRPO's (r_i - m_g)/(s_g + eps) uses the CURRENT group's s_g -> E[g_hat] not proportional to grad J; Dr.GRPO's (r_i - m_g) = (n-1)/n (r_i - m_{-i}) is unbiased (self-inclusion in a plain mean is only a constant factor).
ideas.variance_argument: Per sample, Var ~ E[(r - E b)^2 w] + Var(b_i) E[w] with w = ||grad log pi(y)||^2 (cross term vanishes because b_i is independent of y_i). RLOO: Var(b_i) = sigma^2/(n-1) = sigma^2/7, i.e. 14.3% inflation over the oracle constant baseline mu_x. Shrinkage with k = sigma^2/tau^2 is the Bayesian posterior mean of mu_x given 7 fresh samples and a prior N(h, tau^2): MSE = sigma^2/(n-1+k), dominating both RLOO (k = 0) and history-only (k = inf). Measured on the 800 saved groups (steps 1-100; each prompt visited 4 times, revisit gap mean 25, range 2-49): group means drift between consecutive visits by RMS 26.6 points (visit 1->2, mean score 2.8 -> 23), 11.5 (2->3), 10.1 (3->4) against within-group sigma RMS 16-18 -> k_opt = 0.35, 2.5, 2.7 (weight on history 5%, 27%, 28%). Empirical proxy sum_i (r_i - b_i)^2 L_i relative to RLOO: history-only 1.57 (much worse), shrink k = 1: 0.977, k = 2: 0.978, k = 4: 1.008, k = 8: 1.09; the oracle mean 0.875 is the floor for ANY per-prompt-constant baseline. So the realistic gain over RLOO is 1-3.5% (approaching ~4% late in training when the drift settles). RLOO is already near-optimal in this regime; this is the cheap, free improvement, not a large one.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Advantages are linear in reward differences: a 0.15-point deviation gives |A| = 0.15/c (~0.008), not GRPO's 2.47. Flat groups: exactly 0 when k = 0; with history on, all 8 samples get the same small A = k (r - h)/((n-1+k) c), zero-mean noise bounded by the weight k/(7+k) ~ 0.27. Scale across prompts: common reward scale (combine with rloo-lagged-scale or rloo-prompt-scale for the scale rule), so prompts with larger reward spread contribute proportionally more gradient, as J asks.
ideas.verl_sketch: Same plugin + compute_advantage wrapper (stable prompt key from data.batch['prompts']) as rloo-prompt-scale. @register_adv_est('rloo_hist'): scores = token_level_rewards.sum(-1); inv = np.unique(index, return_inverse=True)[1]; loo = (bincount(inv, scores)[inv] - scores)/(n-1) as in rloo_vectorized (core_algos.py:720-755); h = HIST.get(key); b = ((n-1) loo + k h)/(n-1+k) where history exists else loo; return ((scores - b)/c)[:, None] * response_mask twice. AFTER computing advantages update module-level HIST[key] = (ema_mean, ema_var, n_visits) and the global sigma2/tau2 estimates that define k. Persist HIST to <default_local_dir>/adv_history.json at save_freq (a resume without it falls back to RLOO until each prompt is revisited -- still unbiased). Hyperparameters k, beta, c via env vars. Tune k/beta offline first with the variance proxy: scratchpad baseline_variance_proxy.py (reads outputs/rollout_data_synthetic/*.jsonl).
ideas.risks: Gain is small (1-3.5%) and zero in the first epoch (no history); drift is largest exactly when the policy improves fastest, and a too-large k is worse than RLOO (measured 1.008 at k = 4, 1.09 at k = 8) -- set k from measured drift, not by feel. Stale-history failure mode: a prompt jumping from flat-0 to flat-100 gives all 8 samples A = k*100/((7+k) c) (zero-mean but concentrated noise). History is driver-local state: must be checkpointed and keyed on padding-free prompt ids. Requires the constant-denominator aggregation; under the running per-sequence token-mean a nonzero baseline induces the length gradient of audit item (3a).

ideas.name: Lagged gradient-norm normalizer: scale advantages by an EMA of PAST steps' raw policy-gradient norm (normalized-gradient descent with a one-step-lagged, hence unbiased, normalizer)
aliases: what Adam and the clip actually see
ideas.formula:
Driver state: Gbar = EMA of the RAW policy-gradient norm (the norm the step would have had with scale 1), init from the baseline (e.g. Gbar_0 = 0.3 s0 if measured with reward-unit advantages).
Step t:
  a_t = g_target / max(Gbar_{t-1}, G_min)             # g_target e.g. 0.25 (baseline median grad norm); G_min a fixed floor
  A_i = a_t (r_i - mean_{-i})                          # LOO-centred, reward units, one scalar a_t for the whole batch
After the actor update, read actor/grad_norm_t (the pre-clip norm):
  raw_t = grad_norm_t / a_t                            # undo this step's scale (KL-term contribution ignored; coef 0.001)
  Gbar_t = beta Gbar_{t-1} + (1-beta) raw_t            # skip the update on steps with no non-flat group
Driver-only proxy when the actor's norm is not fed back: raw_t ~ sqrt( sum_i (r_i - b_i)^2 L_i ) / (G S) under token-sum aggregation (independence heuristic), computable inside the estimator.
Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with constant S.
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: J, kappa = a_t/(G S). a_t is a function of past gradient norms (hence of past batches and theta_1..theta_{t-1}) and fixed hyperparameters, never of the current samples. Equivalently: normalized gradient descent whose normalizer is lagged one step instead of being the current batch's own norm (the current-batch version -- what frequent gradient clipping degenerates into -- is a sample-dependent scale and biased).
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: a_t is F_{t-1}-measurable (grad_norm_{t-1} is a deterministic function of batch t-1 and theta_{t-1}; the EMA is a function of all of them). Conditional on F_{t-1}: E[g_hat | F_{t-1}] = a_t/(G S) E[sum_i (r_i - b_i) S_i] = a_t/(G S) grad J by the LOO argument. What is NOT allowed and why this differs from clipping: clip_grad_norm_ multiplies the gradient by min(1, 1/||g_t||), a function of the current batch; when it fires on most steps (as raw Dr.GRPO on 0-100 rewards would: ~18x GRPO's gradients -> norms 2-9 against a clip of 1.0) the update is g_t/||g_t||, whose expectation is not proportional to grad J. Lagging the normalizer by one step restores unbiasedness at the cost of a one-step tracking error.
ideas.variance_argument: Within a step identical to rloo-lagged-scale (one scalar per batch). Across steps it targets the quantity that matters after Adam: Adam cancels any constant kappa, so a scale acts only through (i) the grad_clip threshold and (ii) the PG:KL ratio, both statements about gradient norm, not reward std. Reward-unit scaling misses the length-driven drift of the gradient norm: per-step mean response length went 14k -> 6.7k tokens over 105 steps (p10 6.2k, p90 15k), a ~2x change in gradient scale under sum aggregation that Adam's beta2 = 0.999 cannot track and that a reward-std EMA does not see at all. Under lagged reward scaling the grad-scale proxy still varies p90/p10 = 2.3-2.7 across steps; normalizing by a lagged norm EMA (beta ~ 0.9) removes the slowly varying part (length drift, entropy drift) and leaves only step-to-step sampling noise. With g_target = 0.25 and clip = 1.0 the clip fires only when a step's raw norm exceeds 4x the trailing EMA -- at most a few percent of steps from the measured spread. It also makes kl_loss_coef = 0.001 a stable relative weight: the PG gradient norm is held near g_target, so the KL gradient's share does not drift with length or reward scale.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Same linearity in reward gaps as rloo-lagged-scale (small gaps -> small advantages, large wins uncapped, flat groups -> 0), since a_t is a single scalar per batch. The most scale-free of the scale rules: invariant to the reward's units (0-1 or 0-100), to the aggregation constant S and to the response-length regime -- all absorbed into Gbar -- so the same g_target carries across tasks and reward definitions without retuning s0 or S. Across prompts it keeps J's reward-unit weighting.
ideas.risks: (1) Degenerate feedback when the PG signal vanishes: an all-flat step has raw norm ~ KL-only (tiny), the EMA shrinks, and the next informative step is amplified by up to g_target/G_min -- the floor G_min and skipping the EMA update on steps with no non-flat group are essential (both remain functions of the past). (2) The measured norm includes the KL term (coef 0.001) and any entropy term; a separate pg-only norm would need a second backward, so raw_t is approximate. (3) One-step lag on a quantity that depends on theta_{t-1}: a sudden norm change (e.g. a length collapse) hits the clip once before the EMA adapts. (4) With several mini-batches per step the reported norm is a mean over mini-batches -- still F_{t-1}-measurable, just noisier. (5) It fixes the gradient norm rather than the reward scale, so the effective learning rate no longer grows when the policy finds large reward gaps -- intended for stability, but 'big win' steps are not bigger steps. (6) Monkey-patching the logger is fragile across verl upgrades; the proxy fallback avoids it.

ideas.name: Prefix-branching (paired / antithetic) sampling with sibling-LOO baselines: a VinePPO/TreeRL-style tree estimator that stays unbiased
ideas.formula:
For prompt x: sample m prefixes z_a of at most T0 tokens (a = 1..m), then k continuations c_{a,b} ~ pi(. | x, z_a) per prefix, m k = n = 8 (e.g. m = 4, k = 2 or m = 2, k = 4). y_{a,b} = (z_a, c_{a,b}) ~ pi(. | x) marginally. Rewards r_{a,b}; rbar_a = (1/k) sum_b r_{a,b}.
  Sibling baseline (state-dependent):  b_{a,-b} = (1/(k-1)) sum_{b' != b} r_{a,b'}
  Prefix baseline:                      b_{-a}   = (1/(m-1)) sum_{a' != a} rbar_{a'}
Per-token advantage of sequence (a,b):
  A_{a,b,t} = (r_{a,b} - b_{-a}) / k        for t <= |z_a|   (prefix tokens; the k copies sum to rbar_a - b_{-a})
  A_{a,b,t} = (r_{a,b} - b_{a,-b})          for t >  |z_a|   (continuation tokens)
then / c (or a legal w(x)) and seq-mean-token-sum-norm. If a prefix hits EOS before T0 it has no continuation and its k 'children' are identical copies; the formulas still hold (continuation part empty).
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: Write J_x = E_z[Q(z)], Q(z) = E_{c|z}[r]. grad J_x = E_z[Q(z) grad log pi(z)] + E_z E_{c|z}[r(z,c) grad log pi(c|z)]. Prefix part: the sum over the k copies of the prefix-token advantages equals (rbar_a - b_{-a}); E[rbar_a | z_a] = Q(z_a) and b_{-a} depends on other prefixes only, independent of z_a, so E[(rbar_a - b_{-a}) grad log pi(z_a)] = E_z[Q(z) grad log pi(z)]. Continuation part: b_{a,-b} depends on z_a (the state) and on sibling continuations, which are independent of c_{a,b} given z_a, so E[(r_{a,b} - b_{a,-b}) grad log pi(c_{a,b}|z_a) | z_a] = E_{c|z}[r grad log pi(c|z)]. Both baselines are legal by the stated rule (state y_<t and other samples, never own future). Each prefix token's score is counted once because the k copies carry 1/k of the prefix advantage. Needs a constant loss normalization (seq-mean-token-sum-norm) so the k copies really sum; under the per-sequence token-mean the 1/L bias of audit item (3a) reappears.
ideas.variance_argument: Continuation advantages have variance Var(r | x, z) (within-prefix) instead of Var(r | x): the between-prefix share of the reward variance is removed by conditioning on the prefix, which for competitive programming (approach fixed early) can be most of it. This is the common-random-numbers / paired-comparison effect: siblings share the prefix, so r_{a,1} - r_{a,2} isolates the effect of the continuation. The prefix part uses rbar_a (variance Var(Q(z)) + Var(r|z)/k) against an (m-1)-sample baseline, so with m = 2 the prefix gradient is noisier than RLOO's (only one other prefix); m = 4, k = 2 is the balanced default. Generation cost falls because prefixes are shared (vLLM prefix caching). The sibling-vs-prompt variance ratio is measurable offline from one saved run by sampling continuations from truncated prefixes.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Pairing is where continuous partial credit shines: two continuations of the same prefix rarely tie on a 0-100 judge (they differ on a few tests), so sibling differences are an informative, small-magnitude signal, whereas with binary rewards siblings mostly tie and the pair is wasted. Tiny gaps between siblings stay tiny (no per-pair normalization); flat pairs / prefix groups give 0.
ideas.verl_sketch: A rollout change, not an estimator-only change: two-stage generation in the rollout worker (or a custom generate_sequences wrapper): (1) generate m prefixes per prompt with max_tokens = T0 (e.g. 1/4 of the median response length; record the stop reason); (2) for each prefix build prompt+prefix and generate k continuations, concatenate, and record prefix_len and a parent id per sequence in non_tensor_batch. Advantage: register_adv_est('tree_rloo') taking prefix_len and parent ids from non_tensor_batch (forwarded through the compute_advantage wrapper): group by uid for b_{-a}, by parent for b_{a,-b}, build the (bs, T) advantage tensor with the prefix/continuation split by prefix_len, then / c. old_log_probs / ref_log_probs are computed on the concatenated sequence as usual. Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm; divide the KL on shared prefix tokens by k (or accept k-fold KL weight there). Validate offline first with the inference script (sample continuations from truncated prefixes of saved rollouts and measure Var(r|x,z)/Var(r|x)).
ideas.risks: Largest engineering lift of the set (rollout path, bookkeeping, checkpointing of the new fields); reduced prompt-level diversity (only m distinct prefixes), which can hurt exploration and makes the prefix-token gradient noisier; T0 is a new hyperparameter (too short -> siblings nearly independent, little gain; too long -> prefix dominates, continuation part small); KL loss on the shared prefix tokens is counted k times unless divided by k; token-varying advantages interact with PPO clipping if clipfrac ever becomes non-zero and with any code assuming one scalar per sequence (metrics reading advantages[:,0], rollout dumps). TreeRL / Tree-GRPO define advantages differently (mixing global and local terms) and their unbiasedness was not verified -- do not copy their formulas without the accounting above.

ideas.name: Leave-one-out length / variance-weighted baseline (OPO and this fork's OTB made unbiased, sequence- and position-level) with a past-data go/no-go gate
aliases: Leave-one-out optimal (variance-weighted) baseline: OPO / OTB made unbiased
survival-conditioned LOO baseline (W = 1 position-level special case)
ideas.formula:
Variance-optimal constant baseline per prompt: b*(x) = E[r ||grad log pi(y|x)||^2] / E[||grad log pi(y|x)||^2]. Proxy u_j for ||grad log pi(y_j)||^2 under the aggregation actually used:
  token-sum aggregation (seq-mean-token-sum(-norm)):  u_j = L_j  (OPO)   or  u_j = sum_t (1 - 2 pi_jt + sum_v pi_jt(v)^2)  (OTB, needs actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True)
  per-sequence token-mean (what runs today):           u_j = 1/L_j   (the 'optimal' weight inverts -- fix the aggregation first)
Sequence level:  b_{-i} = sum_{j != i} u_j^alpha r_j / sum_{j != i} u_j^alpha,   alpha in [0,1] fixed before the step (alpha = 0 -> RLOO; alpha = 1 -> LOO-OPO);   A_i = (r_i - b_{-i}) / c
Position level:  W_{j,t} = sum_{s<=t} w_js (cumulative token weights; W = 1 gives the survival-conditioned baseline);  b_{-i,t} = sum_{j != i, L_j > t} W_{j,t} r_j / sum_{j != i, L_j > t} W_{j,t};  fallback b_{-i,t} = b_{-i} when no other sample is alive at t;   A_{i,t} = (r_i - b_{-i,t}) / c  (a genuine (bs, T) tensor)
Gate from PAST data: alpha = 1 if rho_hat^2(r, u) over the previous K steps > 1/(n-1) = 0.143, else 0.
Scale c (fixed or lagged) and constant S as in rloo-const; with rloo-prompt-scale's w(x), J_w.
ideas.objective_unbiased_for: J, kappa = 1/(G S c), for any alpha (and any gate decision) fixed before the step; with a past-data w(x), J_w. verl's shipped OPO and OTB are NOT unbiased (see argument).
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: b_{-i} depends on (x, {r_j, u_j}_{j != i}, alpha) only; the other samples are independent of y_i given x, so E[b_{-i} grad log pi(y_i|x)] = E[b_{-i}] E[grad log pi(y_i|x)] = 0 and the reward term gives grad J_x. Position level: b_{-i,t} depends on t and on others only; 'alive at t' for the OWN sample is determined by the prefix (at token t we already know L_i > t), and for each t, E[1{t <= L_i} b_{-i,t} grad log pi(y_it | y_i<t)] = b_{-i,t} E_prefix[1{alive} E_{y_t|prefix}[grad log pi(y_t|prefix)]] = 0 because the inner expectation is zero at every state. Audit: verl OPO (core_algos.py:528-579) uses b_g = sum_j L_j r_j / sum_j L_j INCLUDING the sample's own (L_i, r_i); unlike the plain mean, the own term enters nonlinearly through the denominator, so it does not reduce to a constant times a LOO quantity -> biased, O(1/n) and length-correlated: E[b grad log pi(y_i)] = grad E[r_i L_i / sum_j L_j] + denominator terms != 0 (toy MC, n = 8, lengths 300-2000: residual 5.1%, 50x the MC floor, cosine 0.9987; the LOO version sits at the floor). verl OTB (core_algos.py:758-873) is biased twice: its W_t cumsum includes the current token's own 1 - 2 pi_t + sum pi^2 (a function of the action y_t) and the group sum includes the own trajectory; its handle_zero_tail=True replaces the baseline by 0 on the tail of the longest response, which with r in [0,100] injects an advantage ~r on exactly the tokens that make a response long -- unbiased but a large length-correlated variance term; the LOO fallback to b_{-i} fixes that. Illegal variants to avoid: using L_i as a feature, the own current token's statistics, or the own full-response features.
ideas.variance_argument: With b_{-i} independent of y_i: Var ~ E[(r - beta)^2 u] + Var(b_{-i}) E[u], beta = E b_{-i}. Moving beta from mu to b* gains Cov(r,u)^2/E[u] = rho^2 sigma_r^2 CV_u^2 E[u]; estimating a u-weighted mean from n-1 samples costs Var(b_{-i}) ~ sigma^2 E[u^2]/((n-1) E[u]^2), i.e. an extra sigma^2 CV_u^2 E[u]/(n-1) over RLOO. Net rule: LOO-weighting beats RLOO iff rho(r,u)^2 > 1/(n-1) = 0.143, i.e. |rho| > 0.38 at n = 8. Measured within-group corr(r, L): mean -0.12, median -0.15 (sample rho^2 mean 0.19, barely above the null expectation 0.14); within-group CV(L) = 0.32. Empirical proxy sum (r - b)^2 L relative to RLOO: alpha = 1 -> 1.017, alpha = 0.5 -> 1.005 (with u = 1 weights: 1.029 / 1.009); survival-conditioned position-level (W = 1) -> 1.046 (worse: 'has not stopped by t' explains ~2% of within-group reward variance while the baseline is estimated from fewer samples as t grows; 2% of tokens have no other sample alive and fall back). So in this task it is a small net LOSS (1-5%); it pays only if length-reward coupling grows (e.g. truncation at the budget scoring 0, or a strong length bias), which the past-data gate detects. OTB's W is the exact expected squared norm of the logit-space score 1[v = y] - pi, discounting near-deterministic tokens that carry no gradient; the optimality model (orthogonal, equal-norm token scores) is crude, so treat b* as a heuristic weighting whose unbiasedness, not optimality, is guaranteed.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Linear in reward; flat groups -> exactly 0 at all positions (any weighted mean of equal numbers is that number); no amplification of small spreads; a weighted mean uses the continuous values fully (binary rewards make b* nearly the mean anyway). Aggregation note: under L-weighting the baseline leans toward long responses' rewards (which score lower here, corr -0.15), so short responses get slightly more negative advantages than under RLOO -- dynamics, not bias. Combine with any scale rule for cross-prompt scale.
ideas.verl_sketch: @register_adv_est('opo_loo') in the plugin; everything needed is in the standard call (token_level_rewards, response_mask -> L_j = response_mask.sum(-1), index): inv = group inverse; ua = u**alpha; S = bincount(inv, weights=ua*r); U = bincount(inv, weights=ua); b = (S[inv] - ua*r)/(U[inv] - ua) with the singleton-group guard; A = (r - b)/c broadcast by response_mask. Choose u = L or 1/L from the configured loss_agg_mode (module constant). Position level @register_adv_est('otb_loo'): per group Wc = cumsum(w*mask) [N,T]; num = (Wc*r[:,None]*mask).sum(0) - Wc*r[:,None]*mask; den = (Wc*mask).sum(0) - Wc*mask; b_t = where(den > 0, num/den, b_seq[:,None]); adv = (r[:,None] - b_t)*mask/c (same shapes as OTB but LOO and without the own-token term). The OTB weight needs actor_rollout_ref.actor.calculate_sum_pi_squared=True plus data.batch['sum_pi_squared'] and old_log_probs, which compute_advantage forwards only for the OTB enum names (ray_trainer.py:203-212): forward them through the compute_advantage wrapper of rloo-prompt-scale (no verl edit). Log rho_hat(r, L) per step and apply the gate. Primary use: the unbiased stand-in whenever OPO/OTB is on a comparison list (never use the shipped versions as 'unbiased' references in ablations), and as a diagnostic.
ideas.risks: Net variance increase of 1-5% at the measured coupling; the ratio-estimator mean is only approximately b* with 7 samples; with u = L the baseline is dominated by long, lower-scoring samples, mildly pushing toward shorter responses (dynamics); OTB's W needs sum_v pi^2 over a ~150k vocab per token (extra actor memory); position-level advantages vary along t, so code assuming one scalar per sequence must be checked; OPO's optimality derivation assumes token-sum aggregation, so under the currently running per-sequence token-mean it is counter-productive.

ideas.name: Prefix-feature state baseline fitted on PAST data (a legal token-level baseline: group-centered ridge regression on prefix log-prob / entropy / position features)
ideas.formula:
At token t of sample i any b_i(t) = f(x, y_i,<t, {y_j, r_j}_{j != i}, past data) is legal.
  phi(x, y_<t) = [1, t/Lbar, mean log pi(y_<t), mean entropy(y_<t), 1[code block started], ...]     (prefix-only features)
  beta fitted (ridge) on PAST steps to predict r_j - m_g(j) from phi(y_j,<t) - mean_{j' in g alive at t} phi(y_j',<t) at random t
  b_i(t) = m_{-i} + beta^T ( phi(x, y_i,<t) - mean_{j != i, L_j > t} phi(x, y_j,<t) ),   with |b_i(t) - m_{-i}| clipped to s_cap (fixed, e.g. 10 points)
  A_i(t) = (r_i - b_i(t)) / c   -- token-dependent, a genuine (bs, T) tensor
Aggregation: seq-mean-token-sum-norm with constant S.
ideas.unbiasedness_argument: The score-function identity holds token by token: E_{y_t ~ pi(.|x,y_<t)}[grad log pi(y_t|x,y_<t)] = 0. For sum_t (r - b_i(t)) grad log pi(y_t|.), any b_i(t) measurable w.r.t. (x, y_<t, other samples, past data) satisfies E[b_i(t) grad log pi(y_t|x,y_<t)] = 0 after conditioning on (x, y_<t, others), while the reward term gives grad J as usual. 'Alive at t' for j != i is a function of other samples; phi(y_i,<t) is a prefix function; beta and s_cap come from past data; the clip is a fixed function of legal quantities. Illegal variants: using L_i as a feature (own future), the own current token's statistics, or centering with the own full-response features.
ideas.variance_argument: The ideal state-dependent baseline is V(x, y_<t); any legal b_i(t) removes the part of Var(r | x) that the state explains, minus estimation noise. Because beta comes from thousands of past samples there is no ESS cost beyond the LOO centering RLOO already pays, so the expected gain ~ within-prompt R^2 of the prefix features -- measurable offline before any run. Length/position alone gives ~0.02 (and the in-group survival baseline is measured worse than RLOO, 1.046x, see opo-loo), so it is worth building only if prefix log-prob/entropy features reach R^2 >~ 0.1. If R^2 is small the estimator is RLOO plus a tiny zero-mean perturbation: safe but useless.
ideas.continuous_friendliness: Linear in r. Flat groups give beta^T(phi_i - phibar_{-i}): non-zero but zero-mean (a shared-prefix contrast), so flat groups contribute pure noise of size ||beta|| spread(phi) -- hence the ridge penalty and the s_cap clip. Across prompts, same reward scale as RLOO (combine with a scale rule).
ideas.verl_sketch: Needs prefix log-probs / entropy: old_log_probs are in data.batch (ray_trainer.py:1236); entropy needs actor_rollout_ref.actor.calculate_entropy=True; forward both through the compute_advantage wrapper (rloo-prompt-scale). Keep beta in the plugin module, refit every K steps from a ring buffer of past (phi, r - m_g) pairs, checkpoint it with the history. Do the offline step first: the rollout dump (trainer.rollout_data_dir) stores only input/output/score, so add old_log_probs (and entropys) to _dump_generations' extra infos (ray_trainer.py:390-420 -- a verl edit, or dump them from the plugin) in a future run and measure the within-group R^2 of prefix features on steps 26-100 before implementing the online version.
ideas.risks: A small critic in disguise: extra plumbing, beta fitted on stale data (policy drift of RMS 10-27 points per epoch can also move the feature-reward relation), token-varying advantages interact with PPO clipping if clipfrac ever becomes non-zero and with any code assuming one scalar per sequence (metrics reading advantages[:,0], rollout dumps). Expected gain is unknown and plausibly small; lowest priority until the offline R^2 is measured.

verdicts.objective: J exactly: J(theta) = E_{x~Unif(D)} E_{y~pi_theta(.|x)}[r(x,y)], with E[g_hat | theta] = kappa * grad J, kappa = 1/(S*c) for the rloo plugin and (n-1)/n * 1/(S*c) for drgrpo (S = rollout.response_length = data.max_response_length, c = 18, n = 8: all fixed hyperparameters). The KL-to-reference term is a separate regularizer outside g_hat and is not claimed to be part of the J estimator.
verdicts.proof_or_counterexample:
PROOF SKETCH (every claim below was checked against the fork's code, not taken from the proposal).

Step 0, what g_hat actually is on the running path. Config (scripts/run_verl_grpo_frontiercs_qwen35_9b.sh and the _synthetic variant): train_batch_size=8, rollout.n=8, ppo_mini_batch_size=8, ppo_micro_batch_size_per_gpu=1, use_dynamic_bsz=false (actor.yaml default), ppo_epochs=1, use_kl_in_reward=False, entropy_coeff=0, temperature/top_p/top_k = 1/1/-1 (rollout.yaml defaults), rollout_correction.rollout_is=null (so no rollout_is_weights are ever added to the batch; the `rollout_is_weights` multiply in compute_policy_loss_vanilla is skipped), legacy worker (fsdp_workers -> DataParallelPPOActor). fsdp_workers.py:248-249 normalizes ppo_mini_batch_size to 8*8/DP, so data.split() yields exactly one mini-batch and dp_actor.py:550 sets on_policy=True -> line 599 old_log_prob = log_prob.detach() -> ratio = exp(0) = 1 exactly; d ratio/d theta = grad log pi. In compute_policy_loss_vanilla the surrogate is max(-A*ratio, -A*clamp(ratio)) then min with -3A and where(A<0,...): at ratio==1 the two clip branches are numerically equal and torch.maximum's tie rule splits the gradient 1/2+1/2, clamp's gradient is 1 strictly inside (1-eps,1+eps), and for A<0 the dual-clip min picks -A (since -3A > -A). So the per-token gradient is exactly -A_i * grad log pi(y_it|x_i,y_i<t): pure REINFORCE, no clipping (matches clipfrac=0).
Aggregation: compute_policy_loss_vanilla calls agg_loss(..., **config.global_batch_info) and ActorConfig.global_batch_info defaults to {} (workers/config/actor.py:184); it is only filled in workers/utils/losses.py:105-108 (new-engine path). So on this path agg_loss gets dp_size=1, batch_num_tokens=None, global_batch_size=None, loss_scale_factor=None. With loss_agg_mode=seq-mean-token-sum-norm and a 1-sequence micro-batch: seq_losses = sum_t loss_mat*mask; seq_mask = 1 (non-empty response); global_batch_size = seq_mask.sum() = 1; loss /= loss_mask.shape[-1] = S. response_mask comes straight from model_inputs (shape (1, response_length)); agent_loop.py:548-566 pads every response and response_mask to rollout.response_length, and rollout.yaml:25 sets response_length = ${oc.select:data.max_response_length,512} = 16000 in both 9B scripts. No trimming of the padded width occurs anywhere between agent_loop and dp_actor (grepped ray_trainer/fsdp_workers/dp_actor; dp_actor.py:362 slices log_probs back to exactly response_length). So S is a constant. dp_actor.py:562-565,585,663: micro-batch loss * 1/G with G = normalized ppo_mini_batch_size / 1 (constant); FSDP reduce = mean over DP ranks (constant 1/DP); _balance_batch only permutes samples into equal-size partitions (get_seqlen_balanced_partitions(..., equal_size=True)), and a sum of per-sequence terms with constant weights is permutation invariant. Hence with N = DP*G = 64:
  g_hat = (1/(N*S)) * sum_{i=1..N} A_i * sum_t grad log pi(y_it | x_i, y_i<t)   (plus the KL regularizer gradient).
Step 1, the advantage. compute_rloo_vectorized_outcome_advantage: adv_i = (c_g*s_i - sum_g s)/(c_g-1) = s_i - mean_{-i} with c_g = 8 always (uid assigned per prompt row before .repeat(n, interleave=True), ray_trainer.py:1438). The plugin divides by the fixed c. For drgrpo (grpo with norm_adv_by_std_in_grpo=False) the code computes s_i - mean_g with self-inclusion; identity: s_i - mean_g = (n-1)/n * (s_i - mean_{-i}). No std, no eps, no batch statistics are used. Baseline b_i = mean_{-i} is a function of x_i and the other 7 samples' rewards only; the 8 samples are independent draws from pi_theta(.|x) (independent vLLM samples; prefix caching does not change the law), and the judge is deterministic given the response, so b_i is independent of y_i given (x_i, y_{-i}).
Step 2, conditional expectation. For a fixed x and any b independent of y: E_{y~pi}[(r(x,y) - b) * sum_t grad log pi(y_t|x,y_<t)] = E_y[(r - b) grad log pi(y|x)] = sum_y (r(x,y) - b) grad pi(y|x) = grad sum_y r pi - b * grad sum_y pi(y|x) = grad J_x - b*0. The baseline term vanishes because the support (sequences ending in EOS before the cap or truncated at exactly response_length tokens) is a complete prefix-free set, so sum_y pi(y|x) = 1 identically in theta; tempering is consistent because dp_actor divides logits by the same temperature vLLM samples at. Applying this to each of the n samples of a group conditional on the other n-1 (tower property) gives E[sum_{i in group} (r_i - mean_{-i}) S_i | x] = n grad J_x, and (n-1)/n * n grad J_x for drgrpo.
Step 3, over prompts. The train sampler is torchdata RandomSampler without replacement with a seeded generator (main_ppo.py create_rl_sampler, data.shuffle=True default, drop_last with 200/8=25 exact), so unconditionally each step's 8 prompts form a uniformly random 8-subset of D: E[sum_{k=1..8} grad J_{x_k}] = 8 grad J. Therefore E[g_hat] = (1/(N*S*c)) * 8n * grad J = (1/(S*c)) grad J since N = 8n. Every factor (1/DP, 1/G, 1/S, 1/c, n, (n-1)/n) is a fixed hyperparameter: no sample dependence survives, so this is unbiased for J in the task's sense, not merely for a reweighted J_w.
NUMERICAL CONFIRMATION (exact enumeration, /var/tmp/claude-1003/-home-shuoyuan-personal-noisy-grpo/83a962cf-965e-4f2a-bf5e-9369212c5246/scratchpad/referee_rloo_const_toy.py): 2 prompts, 3 responses each with lengths [3,1,2] and [1,2,3], rewards [80, 50.15, 50] and [10, 30, 60], tabular softmax policies, n=3, S=4, c=18, all 729 joint outcomes enumerated. rloo-const: E[g]/grad J = 0.013889 on all six coordinates (both prompts), cos = 1.000000, equal to the predicted 1/(S c) = 1/72. drgrpo-const: 0.009259 on all six = (n-1)/n * 1/72. For contrast the currently running path (grpo/std with the de-facto 1/L_i weight): per-coordinate ratios [0.0211, 0.0236, 0.0170, 0.0291, -0.0121, 0.0155], cos 0.932, one coordinate with the wrong sign: a direction bias, confirming the proposal's diagnosis that the two things it removes (std normalization and the 1/L_i weight) are the sources of bias; fixing only one of them leaves cos 0.991 / 0.934 respectively. Replacing the constant S by the batch max length (sample-dependent) already breaks exact proportionality (ratios 0.01852 vs 0.01883 vs 0.01789), which is why the constant denominator is load-bearing. I could not construct any counterexample for the proposed estimator itself; the conditional-expectation argument closes with no residual term.
verdicts.scale_only_bias_factors: kappa = 1/(S*c) with S = rollout.response_length (16000 in both 9B scripts; whatever value is configured it is a constant padded width), c = 18 fixed; times (n-1)/n = 7/8 for the drgrpo variant. The 1/DP (FSDP mean-reduce) and 1/G (gradient_accumulation = normalized ppo_mini_batch_size, dp_actor.py:562-565) combine to 1/N = 1/64 and cancel exactly against the N = 8n expected group terms. All sample-independent. Bookkeeping slip in the proposal: it writes g_hat = (1/(N G S c)) sum_i ... and kappa = 1/(G S c); the 1/G and the DP mean already ARE the 1/N, so the correct constant is kappa = 1/(S c) (toy: 1/72 = 0.013889 observed). Scale-only, does not affect the claim; AdamW absorbs it. Relative to the baseline's per-sequence weight A_grpo/L_i, the new per-sequence weight is (r_i - mean_{-i})/(c S), i.e. the raw gradient per sequence changes by (n/(n-1)) (std_g/c) (L_i/S): not a bias, but with S = 16000 (not 32000) and |A_rloo| uncapped (100/18 = 5.6) the raw grad norm is not obviously 0.3x the baseline's; it can approach the baseline's size on high-spread steps with long responses.
verdicts.hidden_dependencies: Inside g_hat: none found. Checked item by item: baseline mean_{-i} depends only on x_i and the other 7 rewards of the same uid (compute_rloo_vectorized_outcome_advantage); c fixed (env var, measured on past data); std/eps not used; denominator S = loss_mask.shape[-1] = padded response_length, constant (agent_loop.py:548-566, rollout.yaml:25), and global_batch_size = seq_mask.sum() = 1 for every non-empty single-sequence micro-batch; 1/G and DP-mean constants; ratio == 1 exactly (dp_actor.py:550,599) so the clip surrogate contributes no sample-dependent factor; rollout_is_weights absent (rollout_correction.rollout_is = null default); _balance_batch is a permutation into equal-size partitions; uid groups are always size 8; entropy_coeff = 0; use_kl_in_reward = False so token_level_rewards = raw judge score. Outside g_hat but in the applied update: (1) grad_clip = 1.0 is a sample-dependent per-step rescale whenever it fires; with S = 16000 the margin the proposal assumed at S = 32000 is halved and |A_rloo| is uncapped, so it is NOT guaranteed inactive: must be verified on actor/grad_norm and, if needed, c raised (or grad_clip raised) by a constant. (2) An empty response (0 valid tokens) gives 0/0 = NaN in agg_loss (both in the baseline's token-mean and in seq-mean-token-sum-norm), the grad norm is non-finite and _optimizer_step skips the whole step: a sample-dependent zeroing, shared with the baseline and essentially never triggered. (3) Within an epoch the sampler is without replacement, so conditional on the epoch's past steps the prompt law is uniform over the not-yet-seen prompts: a reweighting by PAST data (allowed by the task's definition), marginally J; identical for every estimator. (4) The KL regularizer's per-sequence weight changes from 1/L_i to 1/S (long responses carry more KL); it is a separate objective, not part of J, and the proposal states this.
caveats: Unbiasedness is proven for g_hat as defined (score-function term only). The applied update additionally passes through grad_clip=1.0 and AdamW; clipping, if it ever fires, is a sample-dependent per-step rescale (direction within the step preserved, cross-step weighting distorted). The proposal's '~0.3x baseline grad norm' estimate assumed S=32000; both 9B scripts set data.max_response_length=16000 (rollout.response_length inherits it), and |A_rloo| is uncapped (up to 100/18=5.6 vs GRPO's 2.47), so verify actor/grad_norm stays well below 1.0 or raise c / grad_clip by a constant before trusting the applied gradient.

The constant-denominator property depends on the legacy worker path (global_batch_info never filled). On the new-engine path (use_legacy_worker_impl=disable) losses.py:105-108 fills global_batch_size/loss_scale_factor and actor.loss_scale_factor becomes live; the constants (and whether S is still sample-independent) must be re-checked there.

Correctness of the realised estimator depends on the plugin actually being imported in the driver process that runs compute_advantage; an unregistered name raises in get_adv_estimator_fn, so failure is loud, not silent. Config-only fallback (adv_estimator=rloo, loss_agg_mode=seq-mean-token-sum-norm) is equally unbiased with c=1; only the kl_loss_coef/grad_clip constants change.
Bookkeeping: the proposal's kappa = 1/(G S c) should read 1/(S c) (the 1/G together with the DP mean is the 1/N that cancels the N = 8n group terms). Scale-only; irrelevant for AdamW.

Shared with every estimator and out of scope here: samples come from vLLM's numerics while the differentiated policy is the FSDP model (rollout_correction is off), and the judge is treated as deterministic; and an empty response would NaN the loss and skip the step on both the baseline and the proposed path.

The KL regularizer is re-weighted per sequence (1/S instead of 1/L_i); any constant folded into A must also be folded into kl_loss_coef, as the proposal notes. This is a regularizer design choice, not a bias in the J estimator.

verdicts.objective: EMA / fixed-constant variant (c_t strictly from past steps): unbiased for J, conditionally on the past: E[g_hat | F_{t-1}] = kappa_t * grad J(theta_t) with kappa_t = 1/(S * c_t) (not 1/(G S c_t) as written in the idea; the stray G is a bookkeeping slip, scale-only). Under verl's actual epoch-shuffled loader (RandomSampler, without replacement) the per-step conditional target is grad J_{R_t}, the uniform average over the prompts not yet visited in the current epoch; R_t is F_{t-1}-measurable, so this is a 'reweighting by PAST data' and it is identical for plain REINFORCE/RLOO/GRPO, not something this estimator introduces. Leave-one-group-out variant: exactly unbiased for J with kappa = E_theta[1/c_{-g}]/S under i.i.d. (with-replacement) prompt sampling; under the actual without-replacement 8-of-200 sampling it is unbiased for E_x[w_theta(x) grad J_x] with w_theta(x) = E[1/c_{-g} | x_g = x]/S, a theta-dependent per-prompt reweighting (not the gradient of a fixed objective), whose magnitude on the real 200-prompt spread pool is at most ~1.5% between prompts.
verdicts.proof_or_counterexample: PROOF SKETCH (EMA variant). Fix step t. F_{t-1} = sigma(all data before step t); theta_t and c_t = max(sqrt(v_bar_{t-1}), c_min) are F_{t-1}-measurable because v_bar is updated only AFTER the step's advantages are computed (verl calls compute_advantage exactly once per step in the driver, ray_trainer.py:1566; validation does not call it). Conditional on F_{t-1}: prompts x_1..x_G, responses y_{g,i} ~ pi_theta_t(.|x_g) i.i.d. over i and independent across g, r_{g,i} = r(x_g, y_{g,i}) deterministic. A_{g,i} = (r_{g,i} - m_{g,-i})/c_t with m_{g,-i} = (1/(n-1)) sum_{j != i} r_{g,j} (= (n/(n-1))(r_{g,i} - rbar_g)/c_t, matching verl's rloo_vectorized formula). Applied gradient: with a single mini-batch and ppo_epochs=1, dp_actor.py:550 sets on_policy, old_log_prob = log_prob.detach(), so ratio == 1 exactly and d/dtheta[-A * ratio] = -A grad log pi (both clip branches coincide, and for A<0 the dual-clip min picks the unclipped branch since |A| < 3|A|); seq-mean-token-sum-norm gives g_hat = (1/(N S)) sum_{g,i} A_{g,i} grad log pi(y_{g,i}|x_g) where sum_t grad log pi(y_t|x,y_<t) = grad log pi(y|x). Step 1 (baseline term): E[m_{g,-i} grad log pi(y_{g,i}|x_g) | x_g] = E[m_{g,-i}|x_g] * E[grad log pi(y_{g,i}|x_g)] = (.) * 0, by independence of y_{g,i} from the other samples and the identity sum_y pi(y|x) grad log pi(y|x) = 0, which holds on the length-<=L truncated space (every infinite sequence has exactly one length-L prefix, so truncated-sequence probabilities sum to 1). The baseline depends on x_g and on OTHER samples only. Step 2 (score function): E[r_{g,i} grad log pi(y_{g,i}|x_g) | x_g] = grad J_{x_g}(theta_t). Step 3 (scale): 1/c_t is F_{t-1}-measurable and >= 1/c_min... i.e. bounded, so it factors out of the conditional expectation; it does not depend on any current sample. DECOMPOSITION. With A_i(t) = (r_i - b_i(t))/c and c a constant:
g_hat = (1/(M S c)) [ sum_i r_i grad log pi(y_i|x_i)  -  sum_i sum_t 1[t<=L_i] b_i(t) grad log pi(y_it|x_i,y_i<t) ].

TERM 1 (reward). r is deterministic in (x_i, y_i) and does not involve other samples; the token sum including the EOS/truncation token equals grad log pi(y_i|x_i) exactly. E[r_i grad log pi(y_i|x_i) | x_i] = sum_y pi(y|x_i) r(x_i,y) grad log pi(y|x_i) = grad J_{x_i}. Averaging over x_i ~ D gives grad J, so E[term 1] = M grad J.

TERM 2 (baseline). Fix i, t and let Z_{i,t} = 1[t<=L_i] b_i(t). Let F_{i,t} = sigma(x_i, y_i,<t, {y_j, r_j}_{j != i in group}, past data, theta). Every ingredient of Z_{i,t} is F_{i,t}-measurable: (a) 1[t<=L_i] = 1[no EOS in y_i,<t and t<=T_max], a prefix function; (b) m_{-i} = LOO mean of OTHER rewards; (c) phi(x_i, y_i,<t): constant, t/Lbar with Lbar constant, mean_{s<t} log pi(y_is|.), mean_{s<t} H(pi(.|x,y_i<s)) (H at s = t is also fine, it is a property of the distribution, not of the drawn token), 1[code block started in y_<t]; (d) the alive set {j != i: L_j > t} and the mean of phi(x_i, y_j,<t) over it depend only on OTHER samples (empty-set fallback to the feature term 0 is a fixed convention); (e) beta, s_cap, c are past/fixed; (f) clip(., +-s_cap) is a deterministic function of the above. Samples within a group are conditionally independent given x, so given F_{i,t} the next token is still y_it ~ pi_theta(.|x_i, y_i,<t). Hence E[Z_{i,t} grad log pi(y_it|x_i,y_i<t) | F_{i,t}] = Z_{i,t} * sum_v pi(v|.) grad log pi(v|.) = Z_{i,t} * grad sum_v pi(v|.) = 0. |Z_{i,t}| <= 100 + s_cap so Fubini/tower apply, and E[term 2] = 0.

results.idea_id: prefix-branching (as specified: m=4 prefixes x k=2 children, prefix-token advantage / k)
results.implemented_as: groups of m=4 prefixes (token 1) each with k=2 children (own token 2 + fillers), y marginally ~pi; prefix tokens: A=(r_ab-b_{-a})/k with b_{-a}=mean of the other prefixes' rbar; continuation tokens: A=r_ab-b_{a,-b} (sibling LOO); /18; ssn with constant S
results.notes: BIASED as written: 1.84% = 17x the MC floor (m=2,k=4: cos 0.998800, bias 4.90%, r=[0.985, 1.155, 0.852], relVar 0.866). Cause (confirmed by an independent 4M-tree single-prompt MC): a tree contains only m distinct prefix draws but m*k continuation draws, so E[sum over the n sequences] = m*grad_prefix + m*k*grad_cont; dividing the prefix advantage by k under-weights the prefix (shared-token) gradient by exactly k (kappa on the prefix part = m, on the continuation part = m*k; on the D=0 prompt, where continuations carry no reward, it is exactly proportional with kappa=m). The bias is small here only because continuations carry little reward variance in the toy; in an LLM it is a direction bias between early- and late-token gradients. The idea's 'each prefix token counted once' accounting is the error.

results.implemented_as: every sequence carries the full (r_ab-b_{-a}) on its prefix tokens and (r_ab-b_{a,-b}) on continuation tokens; /18; ssn
results.notes: kappa=0.004626=1/(S c), the same as rloo-const, i.e. the k copies of a prefix simply ARE k (dependent) samples each counted once. relVar 0.467 (m=4,k=2) and 1.072 (m=2,k=4): the pairing gain is exaggerated by the toy's filler tokens (continuation advantages are sibling differences of a few points instead of ~25), and m=2 makes the prefix baseline a single other prefix.

results.notes: Unbiased for any alpha fixed before the step: alpha=0.5 bias 0.06%, relVar 1.002. Net variance loss of 0.2-1.7% here (within-group corr(r,L) is weak in the toy as in the data), matching the idea's own 'small net loss' estimate. Contrast verl's own-included OPO above (3.5-3.9% bias).

Control, verl-OTB-style own-included cumulative W with zero tail (own current token inside W_it): cos 0.998976, bias 4.53% (floor 0.19%), r=[1.006, 0.945, 0.909±0.47], within-prompt cos [0.9992, 0.9984, 0.984], relVar 1.262 -> biased, confirming the audit of verl's OTB (exact verl code path not replicated token for token; handle_zero_tail modeled).
