The own-prefix-dependent baseline term was simulated fully explicitly (no Rao-Blackwellization).
results.notes: Legal token-level baseline: bias 0.06% vs floor 0.11%. No variance gain (0.4%) because prefix log-prob features explain almost none of the within-group reward variance in this toy -- 'safe but useless' unless the offline R^2 is substantial, as the idea says.

simResults.monte_carlo_settings: 6000 independent chains x 150 steps, burn-in 30 steps (EMA / per-prompt history / gradient-norm / ridge state built from each chain's OWN previous batches only; all lagged statistics are read before the step and updated after it, verified by the leak controls), i.e. 720,000 evaluation batches of 8 groups x 8 samples = 46M responses; numpy default_rng seed 0; the only randomness is the prompt draw (uniform with replacement; q_t for the IS idea) and the token draws. E[g] is estimated with the filler tokens (positions 3..L) Rao-Blackwellized wherever the estimator's per-token weights provably do not depend on them (all sequence-level estimators, the branching and position-level LOO estimators); the fully explicit gradient g_full (all tokens) is used for the variance, the gradient-norm feedback, the NGD and OTB-own-included controls and the prefix-feature baseline term, and its mean is printed as a cross-check for every row (agreement 0.0-0.2%, inside g_full's own CI). CIs from the 6000 independent chain means: largest per-coordinate 95% half-width 0.07-0.23% of ||kappa gradJ|| (requirement: <2%); MC noise floor on the relative bias 0.07-0.19%; per-prompt block-ratio 95% half-widths ±0.001-0.010 on all three informative prompts for Rao-Blackwellized rows; wider only on the near-flat prompt for fully explicit rows (prefix-feature ±0.05, NGD control ±0.15, OTB-own control ±0.47) and for GRPO (±0.77 / ±1.8 on a ratio of 326 / 784). Variance: trace Var(g)/kappa^2 relative to rloo-const. Wall time ~9 min single-process numpy.
simResults.issues: (1) FINDING: the prefix-branching idea as specified (prefix-token advantage divided by k) is biased: a tree has m distinct prefix draws against m*k continuation draws, so the 1/k under-weights the shared-prefix gradient by exactly k (bias 1.8% at m=4,k=2 and 4.9% at m=2,k=4 here, 17-30x the MC floor; confirmed by an independent single-prompt MC where the prefix-part kappa is m and the continuation-part kappa is m*k). Dropping the 1/k (every sequence carries the full (r_ab-b_{-a}) on its prefix tokens) is unbiased with kappa=1/(S c). The idea's text and its KL remark should be corrected accordingly. (2) The batch token-mean denominator is a detectable 0.5% ratio bias (5x floor) for RLOO/Dr.GRPO -- negligible in practice but not zero; the audit's 'cos>0.99999' claim is slightly optimistic (0.999986 here with lengths 2-12 in a 64-sample batch). (3) reinforce_plus_plus_baseline gives a nonzero expected gradient on a prompt with gradJ_x=0 (all-equal rewards), in addition to a 5.6x amplification of the near-flat prompt. (4) rloo-hist-baseline: folding the current group mean into h is only a constant rescale (kappa 0.9% lower), not a direction bias, because the self-term is linear; the idea's 'only way to break this' statement is inaccurate (though the prescribed update order is still right). By contrast a 1.25%-per-group leak of the current step into the lagged SCALE EMA produced a real 2-2.5% cross-prompt reweighting (0.69% residual, 7.7x floor), so lagging the scale strictly matters. (5) In this toy GRPO's bias is dominated by cross-prompt reweighting (near-flat prompt x326 relative to J, spread~10 prompt x2.5) with within-prompt cosines 0.998 on the spread prompts; its per-prompt structure (6 approaches with distinct rewards, plus a small detail modifier) is coarse, so within-prompt direction bias magnitudes should not be over-read. (6) Toy limitations: K=4 prompts drawn with replacement (so a prompt can appear twice per batch and histories accumulate ~2 visits/step, faster than the 1 visit/25 steps of the real run); the detail-token modifier is small (<=3.6 points) so continuations carry little reward variance -- this understates the branching bias magnitude and overstates the branching variance gain (relVar 0.45 driven by filler tokens); the lagged-gradnorm raw norm has no KL contribution; the leave-one-group-out scale costs 18% variance here only because 7 other groups (2 flat on average) is a noisy estimate; verl's OTB was modeled (own-included cumulative W, zero tail) but not replicated line by line; the 'cross-fit' prompt-scale variant has exact per-prompt direction but a theta-dependent weight and is labeled 'biased' strictly per the task's definition; 'stm' rows model the legacy per-sequence token-mean path the audit says is actually running. (7) All fitted kappas equal the predicted constants (1/(S c), (7/8)/(S c), 1/S) to 3 significant digits for every row judged unbiased.

simResults.environment_description: Variant B toy. K=6 prompts; a response is a sequence of 1-3 tokens from vocab {0,1,2,EOS}: (EOS)[L=1], (a,EOS)[L=2], (a,b,EOS)[L=3], (a,b,c)[L=3, truncated at TMAX=3 without EOS] -> 40 responses per prompt, 13 prefix states x 4 logits = 52 parameters per prompt, D=312. Policy pi(y_t|x,y_<t)=softmax(theta[x,state(y_<t),:]) with theta ~ N(0,0.8) (EOS logit at the root -1.5). Tokens are modelled EXPLICITLY (choice stated in the docstring): sum_t grad log pi(y_t|x,y_<t) is the sum of per-token softmax scores e_{y_t}-pi(.|state_t), one parameter row per visited state; NOT the 'L identical tokens' shortcut, so position-dependent baselines are real and lengths differ. Rewards r(x,y) in [0,100], deterministic. Under the policy: prompt 0 near-flat (scores 50/50.15/50.3/49.9, within-prompt sigma=0.044), prompt 1 spread 24.3 (corr(r,L)=+0.15), prompt 2 all-equal (sigma 0, grad J_x = 0), prompt 3 spread 12.8 (corr -0.26), prompt 4 bimodal 0/100 plus small partial credit (sigma 18.7, mean reward 4.1, corr +0.32), prompt 5 spread 12.5 with a strong length penalty (corr -0.69). E[L] 2.0-2.8; 36% of sampled groups are flat. |G| = 10.13 with |G_x| = 0.0072, 8.26, 0, 3.33, 3.18, 3.61. A step: B=8 prompts drawn uniformly WITH replacement from the 6 (E_x uniform over the dataset; duplicates are separate groups), n=8 samples per prompt, N=64 sequences, fully on-policy (ratio==1) so the applied gradient is g_hat = sum_i sum_t w_i A_{i,t} grad log pi(y_it|x_i,y_i<t) with verl's agg_loss weights: token-mean w_i = 1/sum_j L_j (batch total tokens, sample dependent); seq-mean-token-mean w_i = 1/(N L_i); seq-mean-token-sum-norm w_i = 1/(N S) with S = TMAX = 3 a constant (loss_mask.shape[-1]). All randomness is the response/prompt sampling RNG (seed; seed+1 for the importance-sampled prompt stream; seed+2 for the prefix-branching stream). Lagged statistics (EMA of within-group variance, per-prompt variance histories, per-prompt EMA of group means, gradient-norm EMA, the ridge fit of the prefix-feature baseline, the sampler's s(x)) are built from strictly earlier batches via exclusive cumulative sums / one-step-lagged recursions, initialised by 5000 warm-up batches of the same stream.
simResults.exact_gradient_method: Closed-form enumeration: G_x = sum over the 40 responses y of P(y|x) r(x,y) sum_t (e_{y_t} - pi(.|state_t)), P(y|x) = prod_t pi(y_t|state_t); the target direction is G = concat_x G_x = K grad J (J = (1/K) sum_x J_x), kappa absorbs the constant. Verified against central finite differences of sum_x J_x on 12 random coordinates: max relative error 1.15e-5. The all-equal prompt's block is set to exactly 0 (the enumeration gives ~1e-15). Per-prompt blocks are disjoint parameter slices, so per-prompt ratios |E[g]_x|/(kappa |G_x|) and per-prompt cosines are exact decompositions. Statistics reported per estimator: kappa = <E[g],G>/|G|^2; cos(E[g],G); relative bias after best scale = |E[g]/kappa - G|/|G| (= tan of the angle; this is the kappa-normalised form of ||E[g]-kappa G||/||G||); its MC noise floor sqrt(sum_j SE_j^2)/(kappa|G|); a z-statistic = RMS over coordinates of (E[g]_j - kappa G_j)/SE_j, which is ~1 for an unbiased estimator; per-prompt block ratio, cosine, direction-z (with the per-prompt best scale) and 95% CI; trace Var(g)/kappa^2 relative to RLOO under seq-mean-token-sum-norm (= rloo-const).
simResults.monte_carlo_settings: 1,000,000 evaluation batches x 64 sequences (64M sequences) after 5,000 warm-up batches, run on two independent sampling seeds (1 and 2; env seed 0 fixed); every number below is seed 1, seed 2 agrees to +-0.001 in every cell (both logs and JSONs in the scratchpad: sim_b_seed{1,2}.log/.json). Runtime 256 s per seed (numpy, chunked einsum). Global 95% CI half-width of the relative-bias statistic (1.96 x floor) = 0.29-0.37% of kappa|G| for all rows except the cross-fit row (0.51%) -- far below the 2% requirement. Per-prompt block-ratio 95% CI half-widths: 0.2-0.7% on prompts 1,3,4,5 for every row; near-flat prompt 0: +-0.6% for the RLOO-family rows, +-1.0% is-prompt-sampling, +-2.4% per-prompt-scale rows, +-1.7% cross-fit, +-28% prefix-feature-baseline and +-199% GRPO (those two estimators inject noise on that prompt that is 100-1000x its reward signal, which is itself the finding). Kappa relative CI < 0.5% everywhere. For lagged/EMA rows the naive CI treats batches as independent: the numerators are independent across batches and the scale is F_{t-1}-measurable, so the mean is exactly E[1/c_t]G; the autocorrelation of c_t only slightly perturbs the CI. A separate diagnostic (scratchpad/pf_diag.py) ran the baseline-only term of the prefix-feature baseline on 8M prompt-0 groups and 2.4M groups each of prompts 1 and 5, with and without the clip: z_rms 0.86-1.10, i.e. E[baseline term] = 0. A control row with an illegal baseline (own length) is detected at z = 220 (prompt-0 ratio 130, cos -0.09).

results.implemented_as: A_i = (r_i - mean_{-i})/c, mean_{-i} = (1/7) sum_{j!=i} r_j, c = 18 fixed; g_hat = (1/(N S)) sum_i A_i sum_t grad log pi(y_it|x_i,y_i<t), N = 64, S = 3 (seq-mean-token-sum-norm). Dr.GRPO raw (r_i - mean_g, same aggregation) is the ref-drgrpo-smtsn row: identical direction, kappa ratio 15.75 = (n-1)/n * 18.
results.per_prompt_reweighting: constant: block ratios [1.000, 1.000, (flat: E[g]_x = 0 exactly), 0.999, 0.999, 1.000], 95% CI +-0.006/0.003/-/0.004/0.006/0.003; per-prompt cos 1.000 everywhere; per-prompt direction z 0.83/1.28/0/1.06/0.80/1.00
results.notes: Residual 0.0017 equals the MC floor 0.0017 (z = 1.02). Fitted kappa = 3.087e-3 = 1/324 = 1/(S K c) exactly as predicted by the idea's proof (8n/(N S K c)). This row is the variance reference (= RLOO under seq-mean-token-sum-norm). Near-flat prompt gets |A| ~ 0.002-0.008, flat groups exactly 0.

results.implemented_as: c_t = max(sqrt(v_bar_t), c_min=3), v_bar_t = EMA (beta = 0.9, init 18^2) of the mean per-group ddof=1 variance of batches < t (flat groups count 0), updated AFTER the step's advantages; A_i = (r_i - mean_{-i})/c_t; seq-mean-token-sum-norm. results.implemented_as: s(x) = max(sqrt((k0 v_bar + sum past s_g^2)/(k0 + m_x)), s_min = 5) from past data (own stream, same recursion as rloo-prompt-scale); the 8 prompts of step t are drawn with replacement from q_t(x) = s(x)/Z_t; A_i = u(x)(r_i - mean_{-i}), u(x) = 1/(K q_t(x)); seq-mean-token-sum-norm; history updated after the step.

Best variance of all rows.

results.implemented_as: h(x) = EMA (beta = 0.5) over PREVIOUS visits of x of the group mean (undefined on the first visit -> plain LOO); b_i = (7 mean_{-i} + k h(x))/(7 + k) with constant k = 2 (row rloo-hist-baseline-k8: k = 8); A_i = (r_i - b_i)/18; history updated after the step; seq-mean-token-sum-norm.

Variance gain 3.3% (k=2) / 6.1% (k=8) -- larger than the 1-3.5% expected in the real run because the toy policy is stationary, so the history predicts the group mean up to sampling noise and heavier shrinkage keeps winning; under the measured drift k = 8 would be worse than RLOO. Confirms the update-order rule: using h built from strictly earlier batches leaves no self term.

results.implemented_as: a_t = g_target/max(Gbar_{t-1}, G_min), g_target = 0.05, G_min = 1e-3, Gbar_0 = 1; A_i = a_t (r_i - mean_{-i}); after the step raw_t = |g_hat_t|/a_t = the ACTUAL norm of the raw RLOO/seq-mean-token-sum-norm gradient of batch t (pass 1 computes it for every batch) and Gbar_t = 0.9 Gbar_{t-1} + 0.1 raw_t, skipped on steps with no non-flat group; seq-mean-token-sum-norm.
results.notes: Residual at the floor (0.0018), z = 1.02; a_t ranged 0.032-0.072 (raw norm median 1.03) and kappa = E[a_t]/(S K) = 2.639e-3. The one-step lag makes the normaliser F_{t-1}-measurable; the toy confirms no bias from the feedback through past gradient norms. +1% variance.

results.implemented_as: Per prompt: m = 4 prefixes z_a = first token ~ pi(.|x, root) (T0 = 1), k = 2 continuations c_{a,b} ~ pi(.|x, z_a) each (n = 8; an EOS prefix has empty continuations and k identical copies); rbar_a = mean_b r_ab; b_{-a} = mean of the other 3 rbar; b_{a,-b} = sibling reward. Token advantages AS STATED: A_{ab,t} = (r_ab - b_{-a})/k for the prefix token t = 0, A_{ab,t} = r_ab - b_{a,-b} for t >= 1; then /18; seq-mean-token-sum-norm over the 64 sequences.

results.notes: The formula as written is biased: with (r_ab - b_{-a})/k on the prefix tokens the k copies sum to (rbar_a - b_{-a}), so the prefix-token term has expectation m E_z[Q(z) grad log pi(z)] while the continuation term has expectation m k E_z E_{c|z}[r grad log pi(c|z)] -- the prefix part of grad J_x is under-weighted by exactly 1/k, and under a per-sequence constant aggregation this is a within-prompt direction error, not a rescaling (z up to 109, both seeds). The accompanying argument ('each prefix token's score is counted once') is the error: each CONTINUATION is also counted once, so the prefix must be counted k times (once per child) to match. Corrected variant (row prefix-branching-fixed): every copy carries the full (r_ab - b_{-a}) (equivalently divide the continuation advantages by k) -> cos 1.00000, resid 0.0020 at the floor 0.0021, z = 0.99, block ratios [1.000, 0.999, 0, 1.000, 1.003, 1.002], per-prompt cos 1.000: unbiased for J. Variance of the corrected tree estimator is 1.45x RLOO in this toy: the between-prefix baseline uses only m-1 = 3 other prefixes and the first token explains little of the reward, so the sibling-pairing gain (Var(r|x,z) < Var(r|x)) does not pay here; with 1-3-token responses T0 = 1 is the only possible prefix length, so the toy cannot evaluate the claimed variance benefit for long responses, only the accounting.

results.implemented_as: Same sampling as prefix-branching; prefix token t = 0 of every copy gets the FULL (r_ab - b_{-a}) (no /k), continuation tokens r_ab - b_{a,-b}; /18; seq-mean-token-sum-norm.
results.notes: Residual 0.0020 vs floor 0.0021, z = 0.99 (seed 2: 0.84). This is the corrected accounting for the tree estimator; the kappa (3.085e-3) matches rloo-const's 1/324, confirming prefix and continuation parts now carry equal weight n = m k.

results.implemented_as: b_{-i} = sum_{j!=i} L_j r_j / sum_{j!=i} L_j (u = L, alpha = 1, token-sum aggregation); A_i = (r_i - b_{-i})/18; seq-mean-token-sum-norm. verl's shipped self-inclusive OPO is the ref-opo-smtsn row.
results.notes: Residual at the floor (0.0018), z = 1.03, whereas the shipped self-inclusive OPO (ref-opo-smtsn) is detectably biased (resid 0.024 = 14x its floor, z = 9.2, per-prompt z up to 12.6 on the length-coupled prompt, block ratios 0.962 on prompt 4 with corr(r,L) = +0.32 and 1.025 on prompt 5 with corr -0.69). Variance +1.9% vs RLOO: the net small loss the idea predicts when |rho(r,L)| is mostly below 0.38 (toy within-group corr -0.26 to +0.32 on three prompts, -0.69 on one).

results.implemented_as: Position-level survival-conditioned LOO baseline (W = 1): b_{-i,t} = mean of r_j over j != i with L_j > t, falling back to the sequence-level L-weighted LOO baseline when no other sample is alive at t; A_{i,t} = (r_i - b_{-i,t})/18 for t < L_i (a genuine (N,T) advantage tensor); seq-mean-token-sum-norm.
results.notes: Residual at the floor (0.0018), z = 1.03: the token-level score identity holds because 'alive at t' for the own sample is prefix-determined and the baseline uses only other samples. Variance +2.7% vs RLOO, consistent with the idea's own measurement (1.046 on the real data) that survival conditioning explains little while the baseline is estimated from fewer samples as t grows.

results.implemented_as: phi(x,y_<t) = [t/Lbar, mean log pi of the prefix tokens (0 at t=0), entropy of the current state, 1[y_0=0], 1[y_0=1] (0 at t=0)] -- prefix-only features; beta fitted by ridge (lambda = 1) on the 5000 WARM-UP batches to predict r_j - mean_g from phi_j(t) - mean_{j' in g alive at t} phi_j'(t) at every token (token-level within-group R^2 = 0.022); b_i(t) = mean_{-i} + clip(beta^T (phi_i(t) - mean_{j!=i, L_j>t} phi_j(t)), +-10) (0 when no other sample is alive); A_{i,t} = (r_i - b_i(t))/18; seq-mean-token-sum-norm.
results.notes: Overall residual at the floor (0.0017, z = 1.00 both seeds). The only ambiguous cell, the near-flat prompt's direction z of 3.4 on seed 1, was resolved by a dedicated diagnostic: the baseline-only term -corr_i(t)/c * score, run on 8M prompt-0 groups (6x the main run) with and without the clip, has z_rms 0.86-0.89 and |E| at the noise level, and z_rms 1.00-1.10 on prompts 1 and 5 -- E[baseline term] = 0, as the token-level score identity requires for a prefix-and-others-only baseline. The seed-1 value is heavy-tailed noise on a prompt where the correction (ridge beta ~ [0, 5.5, 19, -4.3, 2.7] reward points per feature unit) is ~300x the 0.04-point reward signal: exactly the 'flat groups contribute pure noise of size |beta| spread(phi)' caveat. Variance gain only 0.7% because the prefix features explain 2% of the within-group reward variance in the toy.

simResults.issues: (1) prefix-branching AS STATED IS BIASED: the '/k' on the prefix-token advantages under-weights the prefix part of grad J_x by exactly 1/k relative to the continuation part (toy: cos 0.959, per-prompt direction z 60-109, residual 0.29 at a 0.002 floor, both seeds). The idea's sentence 'each prefix token's score is counted once because the k copies carry 1/k of the prefix advantage' is the error: each continuation is also counted once, so the prefix must be counted once per child. Dropping the /k (or dividing the continuation advantages by k) makes it exactly unbiased (residual at the floor); the corrected tree estimator has 1.45x RLOO's variance in this toy because T0 = 1 token is all a 1-3-token response allows, so the toy verifies the accounting but cannot evaluate the claimed variance benefit of sibling pairing on long responses. (2) rloo-prompt-scale-crossfit: per-prompt direction exact and weights equal E[1/(s_{-i}+eps0)] to 3 decimals, but that weight depends on the current theta, so it is 'biased' under the task's definition (as the idea itself flags); it also doubles the variance (2.16x) and gives the bimodal prompt 2.1x weight because s_{-i} = 0 whenever the other 7 samples tie. (3) The RLOO + global token-mean reference (verl's default aggregation) shows a small but statistically clear bias (residual ~1%, 5x the MC floor, z = 3.6 on both seeds) from the batch-token denominator, supporting the ideas' insistence on a constant denominator; the per-sequence token-mean (legacy running path) is grossly biased (residual 27%), and verl's shipped OPO is biased at the 2.4% level (z = 9). (4) Relative-variance comparisons are per 64 generated sequences; is-prompt-sampling and prefix-branching use different sampling schemes than the uniform stream, and the variance numbers for history-based rows (rloo-hist-baseline k=2/8 gains of 3-6%, prompt-scale histories) are optimistic because the toy policy is stationary -- no drift between visits -- so k = 8 beats k = 2 here, the opposite of what the measured drift implies for the real run. (5) The near-flat prompt's exact gradient is tiny (|G_0| = 0.007 vs |G| = 10), so estimators that inject noise on flat groups (prefix-feature-baseline, GRPO, R++) have wide per-prompt CIs there (+-28%, +-199%); for the prefix-feature baseline the seed-1 direction z of 3.4 on that prompt was checked with a dedicated 8M-group baseline-only diagnostic (z_rms 0.86-0.89 with and without the clip) and is noise, not bias. (6) The lagged-statistics rows are evaluated unconditionally (MC mean = E[1/c_t] G); the naive CI treats batches as independent although c_t is autocorrelated; the numerators are independent so the point estimates are unaffected. (7) Toy specifics that differ from the data: within-group corr(r,L) ranges -0.69 to +0.32 by prompt (data: -0.14 on average) to make the length-related biases visible; 36% of groups are flat (data 24%); S = 3 instead of 32000 and K = 6 prompts drawn with replacement (8 per step) instead of 200 without replacement -- none of these affect the unbiasedness verdicts, only the magnitudes of the biased rows and the variance ratios. (8) No files under verl/ were touched; the only new file is analysis/toy_unbiasedness_sim_b.py (logs/JSON for both seeds and the diagnostic script pf_diag.py are in the session scratchpad /var/tmp/claude-1003/-home-shuoyuan-personal-noisy-grpo/83a962cf-965e-4f2a-bf5e-9369212c5246/scratchpad/).
